findings.summary: Corbel's zero-shot nDCG@10 average (40.7) is 4.7 points higher than Dovetail-DR (36.0) across the four evaluated collections, which is slightly smaller than the 5.2-point average gain previously reported for denoised hard-negative mining over standard in-batch negatives on a different six-collection suite.
findings.scope: Average nDCG@10 across Brackwater-News, Felloe-Fin, Moorstone-Bio, Lintel-Law; single training run per system; no statistical tests reported.
findings.caveats: The prior gain was measured on a different set of collections (six vs. four) and included forum and scientific text not in the current evaluation; no statistical significance tests are reported for either comparison.

findings.summary: Corbel outperforms Dovetail-DR on each of the four individual collections, with gains of 4.7 (news), 3.8 (fin), 5.9 (bio), and 4.4 (law) nDCG@10 points.
findings.scope: Per-collection nDCG@10 on Brackwater-News, Felloe-Fin, Moorstone-Bio, Lintel-Law; single training run per system.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; results are from one training run per system.

findings.summary: Corbel also outperforms the lexical reference Lexi-Sparse on average (40.7 vs. 35.3) and on all four collections, with gains ranging from 2.3 (law) to 9.3 (bio) points.
findings.scope: Average and per-collection nDCG@10 on the four held-out collections; single training run per system.

sentences.text: Corbel's average zero-shot nDCG@10 of 40.7 across the four evaluated collections is 4.7 points higher than Dovetail-DR's 36.0, a gain slightly smaller than the 5.2-point average improvement previously reported for denoised hard-negative mining over standard in-batch negatives on a different six-collection suite.
Corbel outperforms Dovetail-DR on every individual collection, with gains of 4.7 points on Brackwater-News, 3.8 on Felloe-Fin, 5.9 on Moorstone-Bio, and 4.4 on Lintel-Law.

Corbel also exceeds the lexical reference Lexi-Sparse by 5.4 points on average (40.7 vs. 35.3) and on all four collections, with per-collection gains ranging from 2.3 points on Lintel-Law to 9.3 points on Moorstone-Bio.
No statistical significance tests were reported for any of these comparisons, and each dense retriever was trained only once, so the observed differences should be interpreted with caution.
